channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold reclaims its footing as Oil retreat blunts Fed shock
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price extends its gains on Friday, edging up 0.89% as Oil prices eased despite renewed concerns of supply shortages and despite a week that featured a rate hike by the Federal Reserve (Fed), which pushed the yellow metal to a nearly two-month low of $4,235.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains against US Dollar, but Fed-SNB divergence weighs
item.description: USD/CHF turns lower on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) loses momentum heading into the weekend, with traders booking profits after a strong weekly advance driven by the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) hawkish interest-rate hike.

item.title: Dollar Index nudges to a fresh high and slips back as Japan raises rates
item.description: The Bank of Japan (BoJ) raised its rate to 1.25% on Friday and the Yen weakened anyway. The Dollar Index ran to its highest level since late July on that and has given the move back, trading just above 100.30.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average gives back its bounce as factory output stalls
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades near 51,500, back at the level where Wednesday's selling stopped, which means Thursday's rebound is gone. The selling ran one way down from the session high, and every level that looked like a floor turned into a step.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens despite BoJ hike as US Dollar remains firm
item.description: USD/JPY advances sharply on Friday, trading around 156.95 at the time of writing, up 0.63% on the day. The pair has pulled back after reaching a daily high of 158.06 earlier in the day.

item.title: Fed’s Schmid supports rate hike as inflation broadens beyond 3%
item.description: On Friday, Kansas City Federal Reserve (Fed) President Jeffrey Schmid said he supported the rate hike, as “recent data suggest inflation trending above 3%.” Schmid added that tightening policy is a step toward achieving the Fed’s 2% goal, that inflation has broadened across a set of goods and servic

item.title: British Pound gives back UK sales pop as Oil shock returns
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) retraces on Friday after reaching a daily high of 1.3375 on upbeat UK data, as headlines suggest that an Oil supply shock has sent crude prices higher and reignited investors' fears of high inflation. At the time of writing, the GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3356, down 0.03%.

item.title: Gold outlook hinges on Oil prices and shifting Fed expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) loses momentum after nearing the $4,400 level on Friday as the Federal Reserve’s hawkish policy outlook keeps the US Dollar firmly supported, while a rebound in Oil prices and US Treasury yields adds pressure on the metal.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Technical setup favours further gains above 100
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) climbs to a fresh seven-week high on Friday, supported by the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) hawkish interest rate hike on Wednesday. At the time of writing, the index trades around 100.40 and is on track to register a weekly gain of more than 1%.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Policy rate seen on hold – ING
item.description: ING economist Charlotte de Montpellier expects the Swiss National Bank to keep its policy rate at 0% next Thursday and over the coming quarters, as Swiss growth has surprised on the upside but inflation remains subdued.

item.title: British Pound: Retail rebound but BoE risks – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes GBP/USD is holding just above recent lows as UK August retail sales beat expectations, reversing July’s decline and firming market pricing for a November Bank of England (BoE) rate hike.

item.title: Canadian Dollar dips as Fed, US yields support the US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD edges higher on Friday, trading around 1.4000 at the time of writing, up 0.10% on the day. The US Dollar (USD) remains supported by expectations of further interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve (Fed), while the rebound in US Treasury yields adds to the Greenback’s appeal.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Pressure builds near 1.40 against US Dollar - Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) remains under pressure near 1.40 against the Dollar, reflecting a firm USD tone and wider US–Canada front-end spreads.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Rate path risks tilt earlier – RBC
item.description: Nathan Janzen at Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) notes that markets are focused on whether the Bank of Canada (BoC) will raise rates in October after the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) move.

item.title: European Central Bank: Quarterly hikes still baseline – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s team sees the European Central Bank delivering two more 25bp rate hikes, in December and March 2027, despite more aggressive market pricing.

item.title: Euro heads for weekly loss against US Dollar on hawkish Fed outlook
item.description: EUR/USD remains on the defensive on Friday and heads for a weekly loss as the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) hawkish policy outlook keeps the US Dollar (USD) firmly supported. A rebound in Oil prices and US Treasury yields adds pressure on the pair.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ hike fails to lift JPY against US Dollar – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Bank’s Danske Research Team notes that the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25% with a 7-2 vote, signalling continued but cautious tightening.

item.title: British Pound: QT overhaul supports Gilt curve and Pound – MUFG
item.description: Derek Halpenny at MUFG highlights that the Bank of England left rates unchanged, but signals suggest a hike is likely in November as most of the majority voting bloc see tightening as needed.

item.title: European Central Bank: One more hike then pause – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Bas van Geffen and Elwin de Groot expect the European Central Bank (ECB) to raise the deposit facility rate by 25bp to 2.75% in December, driven by higher energy price forecasts.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar falls as hawkish Fed stance supports US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD trades lower around 0.5710 on Friday at the time of writing, down 0.3% on the day.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Further hikes supported by resilient economy – Nordea
item.description: Nordea strategists expect the Federal Reserve (Fed) to deliver two additional rate hikes, arguing that resilient United States (US) growth, persistent inflation and continued labour-market strength suggest monetary policy is not yet sufficiently restrictive.

item.title: Euro trades flat against British Pound as UK Retail Sales beat forecasts
item.description: EUR/GBP trades little changed on Friday as stronger-than-expected UK Retail Sales data lends some support to the British Pound (GBP) after it came under pressure following the Bank of England’s (BoE) monetary policy announcement on Thursday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Cautious BoJ tilt weighs on JPY against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights pronounced Japanese Yen (JPY) underperformance, with USD/JPY near 158.00 after a Bank of Japan rate hike to 1.25%. The Bank of Japan (BoJ) signaled cautious tightening, expecting only moderate growth and delayed achievement of 2% inflation.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD extends recovery above $67.00 as yields fall
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades higher for the second consecutive day on Friday, reaching session highs above $67.00 after bouncing from lows near $62.00 earlier this week.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Fresh downside likely if sustain below 1.1455
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is down 0.12% to near 1.1460 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday.

item.title: US Dollar: Oil drives Dollar upside risks – ING
item.description: ING strategist Francesco Pesole notes that moderating Oil prices have slightly cooled the Dollar’s post-FOMC momentum, but still sees upside risks for the Dollar after the Federal Reserve’s hawkish message.

item.title: British Pound: BoE holds but inflation risks linger – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong notes that the Bank of England (BoE) kept Bank Rate at 3.75% in a 6–3 vote while highlighting a more challenging inflation backdrop, with Consumer Price Index (CPI) seen near 3.75% in Q4 and above 4% in early 2027.

item.title: Indian Rupee gets slight relief as rally in US yields and oil price hits pause
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens sharply higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with the USD/INR pair correcting to near 95.75 from an over seven-week high of 96.10 posted the previous day.

item.title: Australian Dollar strengthens as RBA maintains hawkish stance
item.description: AUD/USD rises 0.20% on Friday to trade around 0.7125 at the time of writing. The Australian Dollar (AUD) benefits from hawkish comments by Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) officials, who keep the door open to further monetary tightening to bring inflation sustainably back toward the target.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Yen plummets after BoJ’s policy outcome
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) underperforms its major currency peers on Friday after the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) monetary policy announcement. In the European trade, the USD/JPY pair trades 1.3% higher to near 158.00.
